title: Deep-learning prioritization of metagenomic products yielded cytotoxic compounds
summary: MetasynBGC used gene-cluster-family-guided metagenomic mining and a Chemprop graph neural network to prioritize predicted natural-product structures for synthesis. Six selected NRPS-derived compounds showed in-vitro cytotoxic activity across seven cancer cell lines, with reported IC50 values as low as 38.04 μM; compounds D and E showed cell-line-selective activity. These are in-vitro results and do not establish in-vivo efficacy or therapeutic benefit.
ai_technology: Chemprop graph neural network used to prioritize predicted biosynthetic products by antitumor activity
organization: Shandong University; Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Jining Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary ASM article abstract, methods and author affiliation block checked for online date, model role, synthesized compounds and measured cytotoxicity.

evidence.tested: Six synthesized NRPS-derived compounds were tested in vitro across seven cancer cell lines; the paper reports IC50 values as low as 38.04 μM and selective activity for compounds D and E.
evidence.unknown: No in-vivo efficacy or clinical therapeutic benefit is established. The reported potency is limited to the tested in-vitro cancer cell-line assays.
evidence.ai_role: A Chemprop graph neural network scored PRISM-predicted biosynthetic product structures for antitumor potential; the authors jointly used predicted scores and structural feasibility to prioritize compounds for synthesis and cytotoxicity testing.
